title: waveband-scheduling-retro-2026-11-01
body:
Purpose: quick retro after two weeks of running the waveband scheduling prototype in prod-edge (SFO / EWR) and one dry-run in MAN1. Focus: slot churn, cache-priming efficiency, and regional imbalance.

Attendees: Ravi, Maya, Liu, Aditya, Hannah, Sam (on call), seating: infra warroom

High-level summary:
- Waveband idea: group requests into latency bands and assign slots with soft-priorities to reduce preemption and lower tail latency while increasing packing efficiency.
- Prototype ran from 2026-10-15 -> 2026-10-28 in SFO/EWR; MAN1 dry-run 2026-10-25.
- Win: 95th pct tail latency reduced on large-model traffic by ~140ms in SFO during peak (18:00-21:00 local). Average slot utilization increased from 0.71 -> 0.76 on waveband-configured pools.
- Pain: cross-region imbalance during global surges; MAN1 showed higher eviction churn due to smaller pool sizes and bursty on-demand jobs.

Observations / data points:
- Utilization: SFO pool (g4x-large-1) util 0.76 vs baseline 0.71; EWR saw 0.74.
- Priming index (fraction of requests served from warm KV prefixes): SFO 0.62 -> 0.78 post-waveband for conversational workloads; for embeddings path priming barely changed (0.11 -> 0.13).
- Eviction churn: MAN1 median preemption events per slot/day = 4.1 (vs target <1.5). Mostly caused by opportunistic backfill and our burst policy mis-tagging as long-lived.
- Coldstart latency: small improvement when slot stayed in same band, deterioration when traffic bounced between bands (extra 60–120ms).
- Cost signal: unit token cost down ~3.9% in SFO for waveband groups; EWR cost delta within noise.

Notable incidents:
- 2026-10-21 19:06 UTC: large training job leaked into dedicated pool in EWR. Scheduler honored soft-priority and attempted to move waveband tenants; fallback routing kicked in and sent ~7% traffic to fallback small-quantized model for 7 minutes. Postmortem: INF-3249.
- 2026-10-26: MAN1 dry-run triggered aggressive rebalancer that failed to respect reserve lanes. Resulted in 40m period of degraded QPS for latency-sensitive campaigns. Root cause: rebalancer window misconfigured (60s vs intended 300s) in the staging template.

Decisions made in meeting:
1) Pause expanding waveband to additional non-edge regions until rebalancer back-off logic is tightened and a preemption budget metric exists. (Owner: Ravi; Due: 2026-11-08)
2) Add soft-capacity reserve lanes per region: 3% of slots marked as non-preemptible for 10-minute windows during surge detection. (Owner: Maya; Due: 2026-11-05)
3) Reduce rebalancer aggressiveness: change window to 300s and add hysteresis on slot move threshold 12->20% (Owner: Liu; Due: 2026-11-03)
4) Canary A/B test next week comparing band-based KV affinity vs continuous scheduler affinity for conversational workloads. (Owner: Aditya; Leads: Hannah for metrics)

Action items (explicit):
- Ravi: implement preemption budget metric and dashboard tile (Grafana). Pull request target 2026-11-04.
- Maya: prototype reserve-lane tagging on pool creation path; add e2e test for reserve honoring. Target: 2026-11-05.
- Liu: patch rebalancer: increase window to 300s, hysteresis, and add safety net to avoid moves when pool utilization > 0.9. Deploy to staging 2026-11-02.
- Aditya: run canary A/B with 10% of SFO conversational traffic; gather latency/cost/QPS metrics for 72 hours, report 2026-11-09.
- Hannah: instrument priming-index on a per-band basis, add alert when priming delta < 0.05 after 30 minutes of sustained traffic. Target: 2026-11-04.
- Sam: create runbook snippet for fallback routing observed on 2026-10-21 (INF-3249) and add to oncall playbooks. Target: 2026-11-03.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is 3% reserve lane the right tradeoff for mid-size regions (MAN1)? Need simulation with synthetic burst curves (owner: Maya + capacity). Target sim complete by 2026-11-06.
- For embeddings-heavy workloads, waveband doesn't help priming — should we keep embeddings on a separate class of smaller prewarmed pools? (Owner: Aditya to propose options 2026-11-10)
- How does continued quantization adoption change band boundaries? Need to re-evaluate bands post-8-bit rollout (tentative: 2026-12).

Experiment notes / small tests:
- Pre-warming pacing: tried 30s vs 90s prewarm lookahead; 90s reduced false prewarms by 14% but increased initial tail for sudden spikes. Keep 90s in non-edge for now.
- Soft-priority aging: implemented token-count based aging to avoid sticky low-priority tenants starving. Observed fairness improvement in 3-day backlog test.

Next steps and timeline:
- Short term (this week): rebalancer patch + reserve-lane MVP + Grafana tiles.
- Medium (2 weeks): run A/B canary, collect metrics, iterate on band boundaries per-model-class.
- Long term (1–2 months): evaluate global rollout plan; incorporate quantization/slot-sizing synergy; formalize policy for embeddings partitioning.

Appendix - quick command snippets / refs:
- Rebalancer config in k8s template: infra/k8s/rebalancer-config.yaml (branch: infra/waveband-rebal)
- Canary job run: scripts/canary/run_waveband_ab.sh --region sfo --pct 10 --duration 72h
- Dashboard panels: infra/grafana/waveband-priming-index, infra/grafana/preemption-budget

Notes to self (loose):
- Need tighter Slack alerting for fallback events; current pager is too noisy and hides the root alerts.
- Consider adding a small non-quantized 'search' tier for embeddings-heavy customers to keep latency predictable.

Meeting log captured by Ravi. Will push a short PR to Confluence with the decision list after action items are in Jira.
